item.title: Notes on Orlicz Spaces and Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orlicz spaces are a natural generalization of classical Lebesgue spaces. They are built upon convex growth functions and provide a flexible framework for studying integrability conditions beyond power-type behavior. In this survey paper, we present the basic definitions, main properties, and fundamental results concerning Orlicz spaces, and also discuss the Marcinkiewicz interpolation result for Orlicz spaces.
item.dc:creator: M. Vali Siadat, Wilfredo Urbina-Romero

item.title: Local Hardy and bmo Spaces on Filtered Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of local Hardy and $bmo$ spaces on a connected Lie group with polynomial growth whose Lie algebra is endowed with a filtration. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the local Hardy spaces enjoy an appropriate atomic decomposition, are compatible with Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, and can be identified with certain Triebel--Lizorkin spaces, as it happens in the classical settings.
item.dc:creator: Mattia Calzi, Elena Rizzo

item.title: The convolution product is generally not an open map
item.description: arXiv:2610.38722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the convolution product $\ell^1(G)\times \ell^1(G)\to \ell^1(G)$ is not an open map if $G$ is either non-abelian or contains an element of infinite order. The case $G=\mathbb Z$ solves a problem posed by Kania and Ma\'slany.
item.dc:creator: Felipe I. Flores

item.title: Localization of generators of Markov processes via the Dynkin operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.38761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we consider a Feller process whose resolvent has the strong Feller property. Using the Dynkin operator of this process, we define local realizations of the generator on an open subset $U$ of its state space. In particular, this allows us to describe the generator of the process killed upon leaving a regular, open subset $U$ as a realization of a maximal operator subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Besides the definition via the Dynkin operator, we also consider other possible definitions of such a local realization: a definition in terms of the unkilled semigroup, a definition based on approximation with elements of the generator and a probabilistic definition using martingales. Under mild additional assumptions, we prove that all these definitions are equivalent.
item.dc:creator: Markus Kunze, Jonathan Mui

item.title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.38853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $0<p<\infty$, let $$ G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}, $$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the spectra obtained by passing to subsequences and, for Schauder basic sequences, to normalized successive blocks. Their possible values are exactly $$ \varnothing,\quad (0,\infty),\quad (1,\infty),\quad [r,\infty),\quad (r,\infty)\qquad (r>1), $$ and the possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every admissible pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization, even in the fixed dual $\ell_\infty(\mathfrak c)=\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, and may be realized with empty spectrum for the original sequence. We also determine sharp universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for $p$-strong normality at a fixed exponent, $c_0$ for the whole subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. More generally, for every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal $A\subsetneq c_0$, membership of the error sequence in $A$ is exactly the universal condition preserving density of the $A$-summability domain. Finally, we extend the author's 2012 selection example from exponent one to every $p>0$ and to every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal. The good subsequences are exactly those whose index sets have uniformly bounded runs of consecutive integers; in the good case the detected quotient is isomorphic to $c_0$ and the whole selected sequence is weak-star Schauder basic.
item.dc:creator: Wies{\l}aw \'Sliwa

item.title: Characterization of sets in metric spaces where the big Lipschitz derivative is infinite
item.description: arXiv:2610.38856v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X$ be a metric space without isolated points. In this paper we prove that $E$ is a $G_\delta$-set in $X$ if and only if there exists a continuous function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ whose big Lipschitz derivative is infinite precisely on $E$. To this end, we introduce a new generalization of the classical Takagi function to the setting of metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jes\'us Llorente, Oleksandr Maslyuchenko, Ziemowit W\'ojcicki

item.title: Exh subspaces of bounded variation spaces generated by submeasures
item.description: arXiv:2610.38891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the present paper we are building one more bridge between the theory of ideals on the set of natural numbers and the theory of spaces of functions of bounded variation. It is already known that $F_\sigma$ ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Fin}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a nice generalization of different concepts from the theory of functions of bounded variation (Waterman variation and Chanturya classes). In this paper we show that analytic P-ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Exh}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a generalization of spaces of functions continuous in $\Lambda$-variation. The properties of this generalization are investigated.
item.dc:creator: Jacek Gulgowski, Adam Kwela, Pawe{\l} Sawicki, Jacek Tryba

item.title: Coarse comparison of Bessel families
item.description: arXiv:2610.39002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify Bessel families in separable Hilbert spaces under coarse equivalence relations: $f$ and $\tilde f$ are equivalent if the seminorms $\|T_f\,\cdot\|$ and $\|T_{\tilde f}\,\cdot\|$ of their analysis operators are mutually dominated, up to constants, after pullback along operators $w,\tilde w$ of a prescribed class $\mathcal O$. In contrast with orbit relations such as unitary or similarity equivalence, these relations ignore redundancy and the geometry of the index set, and compare frames, nonframes and compact families on the same footing. They are level $-1$ of the comparison categories of the companion article, and we compute the levels $0$ and $k\ge1$: they are trivial for bounded, injective, bounded below, isometric and upper semi-Fredholm comparison operators, and for invertible or unitary ones level $1$ is a stabilizer-type group of the family. For bounded $\mathcal O$ the classes are given by the singular numbers up to constants; injective operators add the kernel dimension, bounded below operators or isometries add upper semi-Fredholmness, and invertible, unitary or surjective operators give the kernel dimension and the dyadic multiplicity sequence of the spectrum up to bounded displacement on the logarithmic scale, which splits each remaining class into continuum many. Upper semi-Fredholm operators give only three noncompact classes, whereas Fredholm operators give continuum many, so that the Fredholm relation is strictly finer. For each relation we determine exactly which families are equivalent to an orthonormal basis, and we compute an operator Banach--Mazur distance, $\log(\sup_ns_n/\tilde s_n\cdot\sup_n\tilde s_n/s_n)$. As applications, we obtain a relative Paley--Wiener stability theorem for Bessel families and the invariance of Schatten membership and of $\int\|f\|^2$ under coarse equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Nizar El Idrissi

item.title: Additive preservers of mutual strong numerical radius orthogonality
item.description: arXiv:2610.39080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with $\dim H\ge2$. We show that the additive surjections on $\mathcal{B}(H)$ and on its self-adjoint part $\mathcal{B}_s(H)$ that preserve mutual strong numerical-radius orthogonality in one direction are precisely the maps of the form $A\mapsto cUAU^*$, where $U$ is a unitary or antiunitary operator on $H$ and $c$ is a nonzero complex or real scalar, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Yulong Tian, Jinli Xu

item.title: Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.39131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a H\"{o}lder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fr\'{e}chet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.
item.dc:creator: Akari Ishida, Sei Nagayasu

item.title: On an affirmative solution to Michael's problem, with applications to automatic continuity theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1952, Michael posed a question about functional continuity of commutative Fr\'{e}chet algebras in his memoir, known as Michael's problem in the literature. We settle this in the affirmative along with its equivalent forms. Indeed, we continue our previous works to directly attack these problems. We show that the test case for this problem -- the Fr\'{e}chet algebra $\cal U$ of all entire functions on $\ell^\infty$ -- is, in fact, a Fr\'{e}chet algebra $\cc[[X]]$, if there exists a discontinuous character on $\cal U$. An important tool is a topological version of the tensor (symmetric) algebra over a Banach space. The elementary, but crucial, idea is to express the test algebra $\cal U$ as a {\it weighted Fr\'{e}chet symmetric algebra} over the Banach space $\ell^1$. We summarize the effects of our affirmative solution in terms of important applications in automatic continuity theory, including affirmative answers to two significant, long-standing problems from 1966 and 1978.
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: Sharp Tilting Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2610.39598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$ and $1/2\le\alpha\le1$, we establish $\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[A\,D\log(A^\alpha+B^\alpha)(B^\alpha)\right] \le s^s(1-s)^{1-s}\operatorname{Tr}[A^\alpha B^{1-\alpha}]$, where $s=(1-\alpha)/\alpha$, with the optimal coefficient. The proof uses a superoperator representation of the directional derivative of the logarithm and an Araki-type estimate for the derivative of a fractional power. Both this inequality and its symmetric-quotient counterpart extend to positive trace-class $A$ and positive, possibly unbounded, self-adjoint $B$ on a separable Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: Hao-Chung Cheng, Po-Chieh Liu

item.title: Riccati Equations and the Third Problem of Halmos
item.description: arXiv:2610.39605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rencently, Fang, Hou, Jiang, and Zhang reduced Halmos's third problem to invertible operators with conjugate bi-geometric form. An operator has such a form if, with respect to an orthogonal decomposition, it admits a representation $$ T = \begin{pmatrix} A & C \\ 0 & B \end{pmatrix}, \quad A^*, B \in B_1(O_\delta),$$ where $O_\delta=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|<\delta\}$ for some $\delta>0$, and $B_1(O_\delta)$ denotes the rank-one Cowen--Douglas class. We restrict our attention to the case $B=A^*$ with strictly positive coupling $C$, and settle Halmos's third problem for this class of operators. More precisely,we prove that every such operator $T$ is invertible and that $T^{-1}$ has a nontrivial closed invariant subspace. This result contributes to the study of Halmos's third problem within the conjugate bi-geometric framework.The proof combines monotone solutions of operator Riccati equations with strong operator convergence to construct invariant subspaces for associated Hamiltonian operator matrices.
item.dc:creator: Kui Ji, Zhenyue Wang

item.title: The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
item.description: arXiv:2610.39769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the P\'olya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the P\'olya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: Higher-order jet and its application to the Novikov conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.40062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the deffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher order $\mu$-discreteness for subgroup $\Gamma < {\rm Diff}(M)$. As applications, we show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher order $\mu$-discreteness.
item.dc:creator: Jintao Deng, Geng Tian

item.title: Rota universality of shifts on trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.40089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider shift operators on infinite directed trees. We prove that under very mild assumptions on the structure of the tree, the resulting operator is universal (in the sense of Rota). We show connections between the spectrum of the operator and the frequency of branching in the tree.
item.dc:creator: Jeremiah Buckley, Daniel Seco

item.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
item.description: arXiv:2610.40118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators.
item.dc:creator: Shubham Jain, Jaydeb Sarkar

item.title: Compact and Hilbert-Schmidt composition operators on weighted Hardy spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lef\`evre, Li, Queff\'elec, and Rodr\'iguez-Piazza [12] recently characterized the sequences $\beta$ for which the weighted Hardy space $H^2(\beta)$ has the same bounded composition operators as the Hardy space $H^2$. We investigate the analogous questions for the compactness and the $p$-Schatten classes: for which sequences $\beta$ does the space $H^2(\beta)$ have the same compact or $p$-Schatten class composition operators as $H^2$?
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Cruz-Zamorano, Eugenio Dellepiane, Daniel Seco

item.title: Positive Toeplitz Operators Between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Fock Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.40236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study positive measure-symbol Toeplitz operators between Gaussian radial--angular mixed-norm Fock spaces throughout the full range of exponents, including infinity. We obtain a complete characterization of boundedness in terms of weighted local masses of the symbol measure, or equivalently in terms of its Gaussian Berezin profile. The criterion separates the transfer of angular integrability from that of radial summability and remains valid in the quasi-Banach and endpoint regimes. We further characterize compactness and obtain the corresponding essential-norm estimates through the asymptotic behavior of the same local-mass and Berezin profiles, and determine the mappings involving the large and little outer-endpoint spaces. We also prove an independent characterization of bounded positive Toeplitz sesquilinear forms. The proofs combine atomic recovery, localized Gaussian matrix estimates, and Rademacher extraction.
item.dc:creator: Deepak K. Dileep, Xiang Fang, Pham Trong Tien

item.title: Perturbations of Truncated Toeplitz operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.40295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structure of kernels of finite-rank perturbations of truncated Toeplitz operators. By realizing a perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator on a model space as a suitable matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator on an enlarged model space, we identify its kernel with a coordinate projection of the kernel of an associated block Toeplitz operator. This realization enables us to transfer the nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of Toeplitz kernels to the perturbed truncated setting. More precisely, for a perturbation of rank at most $n$, we show that the kernel of the perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator is nearly $S^*$-invariant with defect at most $2n+1$. We then extend the method to truncated Toeplitz operators on multiband spaces. In this setting, a perturbation of rank at most $n$ again preserves the finite-defect nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of the kernel, with the explicit upper bound $2n+2$ for the defect.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Arshad Khan

item.title: Diffraction of rotated measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.37992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider a translation-bounded measure on the line. We can rotate the measure, distributing the mass proportionally to the area, to create a two-dimensional rotationally invariant translation-bounded measure. We show that the diffraction of the two-dimensional object is the normalised rotation of the diffraction of the original measure. We discuss some examples and generalisation beyond $d=2$.
item.dc:creator: Jan Maz\'a\v{c}, Nicolae Strungaru

item.title: Stability of a Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.38409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation \begin{align*} \sum_{\emptyset \neq I \subset \{ 1, 2, \ldots, n+1 \}} (-1)^{|I|-n+1} f \Bigg( \sum_{i \in I} x_i \Bigg) = 0 \end{align*} in the sense of G\u{a}vru\c{t}a.
item.dc:creator: Sun-Sook Jin, Soon-Mo Jung, Yang-Hi Lee

item.title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
item.dc:creator: Micha{\l} Kijaczko, Vivek Sahu

item.title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
item.description: arXiv:2610.38500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.
item.dc:creator: Rainer Picard, Sascha Trostorff, Marcus Waurick

item.title: Optimality Conditions and Solution Set Characterisations of Convex Minimal Time Optimisation Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.38553v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The paper studies convex minimisation problems involving a composition of a coordinatewise nondecreasing convex function with a finite family of nonnegative, locally Lipschitz continuous and convex functions. We establish complete dual optimality conditions and characterise the entire solution set using multipliers and subgradients associated with a given solution. The results are applied to norm optimisation problems involving minimal time functions with different convex dynamics sets and convex target sets. The sum, maximum and p-norms yield minimal time versions of the Fermat--Torricelli, Chebyshev centre and p-Fermat--Torricelli problems, respectively. Examples in finite and infinite dimensional spaces are provided to illustrate the solution set characterisations.
item.dc:creator: Doan Huu Hieu, Nguyen Duy Cuong

item.title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.38669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.
item.dc:creator: Samuel A. Ballas, Ferhat Karabatman, Tom Needham, Clayton Shonkwiler

item.title: Homogeneous polynomial approximation on symmetric convex bodies: A proof of Kro\'o's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.38877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve Kro\'o's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kro\'o's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights. Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization. We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook

item.title: Uncertainty principles as forcing mechanisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.38909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note we first consider the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. We show that it acts as a {\bf forcing mechanism} in the following sense. Real functions that approach its limit are close to Gaussian distributions, with proximity both in the sense of total variation distance and Wasserstein-1 distance. We next consider the uncertainty principle for functions defined on finite Abelian groups, and show that it acts as a forcing mechanism in the following sense. Functions that approach its limit are close (after translation and modulation by a complex exponential) to indicator functions of some subgroup, with proximity measured in ${\mathbb {L}}^1$-norm.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Massouli\'e

item.title: Invariant means, coset correct means and the Hahn-Banach Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, in ZF set theory, the existence of "coset correct means" on all groups is equivalent to the Hahn-Banach Theorem, as well as to the existence of invariant means on abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Armando Martino, Motiejus Valiunas

item.title: Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.39164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.
item.dc:creator: Denis Fufaev

item.title: Sharp derivative inequalities for maximal functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.39178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the optimal constant in the $L^p$-derivative inequality for the uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on the real line for every $1<p<\infty$. It is the unique number $\gamma_p\in [0,1]$ satisfying $(2p-1)\gamma_p+(p-1)\gamma_p^{(2p-1)/(p-1)}=p$. As $p$ goes from $1$ to $+\infty$, $\gamma_p$ decreases from $1$ to $\sqrt2-1$, and at the endpoints the limiting arguments recover the classical total-variation and Lipschitz inequalities, with the qualitative regularity ingredient at the $BV$ endpoint supplied by Aldaz and P\'erez L\'azaro.
item.dc:creator: Sung-Yi Liao, Jos\'e Madrid, Eyvindur Ari Palsson

item.title: The functional analytic approach establishes the Corona theorem in the theory of SCV
item.description: arXiv:2610.39425v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an affirmative solution of the original Corona problem (1962) for certain bounded pseudoconvex domains or polydomains in $\mathbb{C}^n$, including the balls and polydiscs, by using the Gleason solvability property of such domains for $H^\infty(G)$. In fact, we establish an equivalency of the Corona problem and Gleason's problem (1964) in the theory of several complex variables. Indeed, we extend our recent works on both problems based on the functional analytic approaches, and extend recent work of Clos, as well as apply the usual Banach algebra method. As an application, we establish the I. J. Schark's theorem for these $G$'s. We also obtain a welcome extension of a result of Krantz and Li (1995) for a bounded, strictly pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $C^3$ boundary.
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: Singularity removal in nonlocal operator inequalities on domains and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.39437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that certain classes of nonlocal integral estimates on domains, involving operators, may be reduced to the local analogues without the singular weight on cubes. The theory applies to two-sided inverse doubling and quasi-monotone kernels with some moment conditions, and with a left-hand-side operator with average domain-bi-Lipschitz properties. Direct applications to fractional semi-norm inequalities in Peridynamics, such as fractional Korn's inequalities and Geometric Rigidity Estimates are presented.
item.dc:creator: Davit Harutyunyan

item.title: On certain mapping properties of a weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.39502v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we study a weighted analogue of the totally geodesic $k$-plane transform on the real hyperbolic space. Throughout the article, we are concerned with the mapping properties of this transform. Particularly, we first consider the existence of the operator on weighted Lebesgue spaces, where the weights under consideration are natural to the geometry of the hyperbolic space. Then, we proceed to see the $L^p$-improving mapping properties of the said transform on radial functions. Further, we also prove end-point boundedness results on Lorentz spaces of radial functions. Lastly, we look into the problem of weighted $L^p$-$L^p$ boundedness, and obtain partial results in this direction. In the way of obtaining these results, we also give a spherical integral representation of the weighted totally geodesic $k$-plane transform.
item.dc:creator: Pratyay Datta, Aniruddha Deshmukh, Ashisha Kumar

item.title: Euler--Lagrange Flow Monotonicity for the Radon Transform
item.description: arXiv:2610.39818v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new gradient-like flow that targets critical points of the inequality for the planar Radon transform $\mathcal{R}$ proven by Oberlin and Stein, partially answering a question of Christ, who gave a complete characterisation of the extremisers of the inequality via rearrangement methods. We show that for non-negative radial initial data near the extremiser manifold, solutions to the flow exist globally and there exists a rescaled subsequence of the flow that converges to a critical point of the Radon functional $\|\mathcal{R} f\|_3/\|f\|_{3/2}$ locally in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We also obtain a quantitative result for the rate of decay of critical points, which complements a result of Christ arXiv:1106.0719 in the special case of radial functions. We prove a novel localised smoothing estimate for the operator $\mathcal{R}^*[(\mathcal{R}\cdot)^2]$ restricted to radial functions. This approach is complementary to that of Christ and provides a robust framework for studying extremal problems associated to Radon-like operators.
item.dc:creator: Yannis Galanos

item.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
item.description: arXiv:2610.39967v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Yang

item.title: Data-driven Regularization for Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.40048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem. In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems. In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions. Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method. For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Oleh Melnyk, Sebastian Neumayer

item.title: Discrete hermitian groups are FC-hypercentral
item.description: arXiv:2610.40226v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that a discrete group is hermitian if and only if it is FC-hypercentral, that is, if and only if it does not have any nontrivial ICC quotients. In particular, a finitely generated group is hermitian if and only if it is virtually nilpotent. The main step is an elementary, self-contained proof that every hermitian ICC group is trivial, based on a finite-set separation property of nontrivial ICC groups.
item.dc:creator: Tron Omland

item.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.40475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound. We present these consequences before the machinery. The main arguments simplify irrational-power finite-rank rigidity and give a Nash-curve ramification obstruction, stable under entire scalar additions, for powers, logarithms, and rational poles. The latter yields uniform finite supports on compact semialgebraic curves without assuming that the supports are semialgebraic. The known p-frame finite-replacement principle is distinguished from the extensions developed here. No unconditional discreteness theorem for general irrational p is claimed.
item.dc:creator: Josiah Park

item.title: On avatars of the Singer-Wermer conjecture in Frechet algebras
item.description: arXiv:2003.13243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct two Fr\'{e}chet algebras admitting countably many mutually inequivalent Fr\'{e}chet algebra topologies. The second example is a modification of the maiden (and first) example of a non-Banach Fr\'{e}chet algebra with two inequivalent Fr\'{e}chet algebra topologies, considered by Read to show that the famous Singer-Wermer conjecture does not hold in the Fr\'{e}chet case. We discuss a couple of avatars of the Singer-Wermer conjecture in Fr\'{e}chet algebras. In particular, this conjecture (and so, its weaker version, too) does hold by the second example which also admits countably many mutually equivalent Fr\'{e}chet algebra topologies. However the stronger version of this conjecture (i.e., the Kaplansky's conjecture) does not hold by the second example.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of ICTAA 2021, Mathematics Studies 8, Estonian Mathematical Society, Tartu, 2021, pp. 121-137
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: On an affirmative solution to the non-commutative Michael's problem, with applications to automatic continuity theory
item.description: arXiv:2006.11134v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1952, Michael posed a question about functional continuity of commutative Fr\'{e}chet algebras in his memoir, known as Michael's problem in the literature. We settle this in the affirmative for the non-commutative Fr\'{e}chet algebras, along with its equivalent form. Indeed, we continue our previous works to directly attack these problems. We show that the existence of a discontinuous character on the non-commutative test case for this problem -- the Fr\'{e}chet algebra ${\cal U}_{nc}$ of all entire functions on $\ell^\infty$ -- allows us to generate another Fr\'{e}chet algebra topology on ${\cal U}_{nc}$, inequivalent to the usual Fr\'{e}chet algebra topology. An important tool is a topological version of the tensor algebra over a Banach space. The elementary, but crucial, idea is to express the test algebra ${\cal U}_{nc}$ as a {\it weighted Fr\'{e}chet tensor algebra} over the Banach space $\ell^1$. We give some important applications in automatic continuity theory. In particular, we provide affirmative answers to significant, long-standing problems from 1967 (extending Johnson's result for non-commutative, semi-simple Fr\'{e}chet algebras; Dales' survey, Question 9), 1976 (extending Esterle's result, giving another approach for Michael's problem for more general $(F)$-algebras), and 1978 (a weaker version of an equivalent form of the non-commutative Michael's problem; Dales' survey, p. 143).
item.dc:creator: S. R. Patel

item.title: Centro-Affine Differential Geometry and the Log-Minkowski Problem
item.description: arXiv:2104.12408v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We interpret the log-Brunn-Minkowski conjecture of B\"or\"oczky-Lutwak-Yang-Zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. In particular, we show that the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine Laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. As every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine Ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted Ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. In particular, we may use the classical argument of Lichnerowicz and a centro-affine Bochner formula to give a new proof of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality. For origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $L^p$- and log-Minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $L^p$- and log-Minkowski conjectured inequalities. As a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-Minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $K$ with $\bar K \subset K \subset 8 \bar K$, so that $K$ satisfies the log-Minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $K$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $V_K$. If $\bar K$ is not extremely far from a Euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+\epsilon$, is obtained as well.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Milman

item.title: Demi Weak Dunford-Pettis Operators
item.description: arXiv:2603.08922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, our main goal is to introduce the class of Demi Weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We also investigate its relationship with the classes of weak Dunford-Pettis and demi Dunford-Pettis operators, as well as conditions under which this class coincide with the classes of demi Dunford-Pettis and demicompact operators. In the final section, we study some properties of this new class in the setting of Banach lattices.
item.dc:creator: Joilson Ribeiro, Fabricio Santos

item.title: Embeddings of variable Sobolev, Besov, and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces on metric measure spaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.19111v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sobolev-type embeddings on metric measure spaces encode a subtle interaction between the analytic regularity of functions and the geometry of the underlying domain space. In this paper we develop an embedding theory for variable Haj{\l}asz-type smoothness spaces on metric measure spaces whose ``dimension'' is allowed to vary pointwise through a bounded exponent $Q(\cdot)$ that governs a lower Ahlfors growth condition on the measure. We introduce variable exponent Haj{\l}asz-Sobolev spaces $M^{s(\cdot),p(\cdot)}$, Haj{\l}asz-Triebel-Lizorkin spaces $M^{s(\cdot)}_{p(\cdot),q(\cdot)}$, and Haj{\l}asz-Besov spaces $N^{s(\cdot)}_{p(\cdot),q(\cdot)}$, and establish Sobolev, Morrey, and Moser-Trudinger type embeddings into variable exponent Lebesgue and H\"older spaces. These embeddings are proved both locally (on balls) under a lower Ahlfors $Q(\cdot)$-regularity condition on the measure and regularity assumptions on the exponents (notably log-H\"older continuity), and globally under additional geometric hypotheses such as geometric doubling and mild uniform bounds on the measure of unit balls. We also identify geometric conditions that are not only sufficient but, in appropriate forms, necessary for the validity of these embeddings, showing in particular that such inequalities force a lower growth bound on the measure of order $r^{Q(x)}$.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alvarado, Micha{\l} Dymek, Przemys{\l}aw G\'orka, Nijjwal Karak

item.title: Universal Closest Refinement on Measurable Bipartite Relations
item.description: arXiv:2604.10274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the universal closest refinement problem on measurable bipartite relations over standard Borel spaces. Given prescribed side measures, the feasible class consists of finite refinement plans concentrated on the relation and carrying one fixed marginal. The main question is whether this highly nonunique class nevertheless contains a mathematically distinguished class of refinements. We show that the correct one-sided extremal criterion is level-optimal maximin, a levelwise maximin principle formulated through truncation and overflow profiles. We then prove that this structure is exactly the one selected by convex refinement: every minimizer of a strictly convex refinement criterion is level-optimal maximin, while every level-optimal maximin refinement minimizes the full class of relevant proper lower semicontinuous convex divergence functionals. Proportional response then identifies the opposite-side partner and yields a universally closest refinement pair. Our main theorem shows that every such pair is universally closest among all feasible pairs for every divergence satisfying the data-processing inequality under measurable post-processing, and conversely that every universally closest pair has this structure. We also prove a converse paired characterization for strictly convex closest pairs. Finally, we give an equilibrium-theoretic characterization of level-optimal maximin pairs through a naturally associated continuum economy with measure-valued commodities. The measure-theoretic theory requires new tools beyond the finite case, including disintegration, measurable selection, measurable max-flow/min-cut duality, augmentation arguments, and a symmetric density decomposition separating absolutely continuous and singular components.
item.dc:creator: T-H. Hubert Chan

item.title: $L^p$ approximation results for infinite dimensional Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2608.08230v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Leveraging the neural architectures which we introduced in arXiv:2109.13512v4, we show a global universal approximation theorem in the topology of $L^p(\mu)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $\mu$ is a Radon probability measure on a suitable infinite dimensional topological space $\mathfrak X$. Namely, any function $f:\mathfrak X\to \mathbb R$ in $L^p(\mu)$ can be approximated to any degree of accuracy by suitable infinite dimensional architectures. These architectures can be in turn approximated by almost classical neural networks which are specified by a finite number of parameters only. The vectorial case (where $f=f(x)\in E$ and $E$ is a Banach space) is also considered and analogous results are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Luca Galimberti

item.title: A class of port-Hamiltonian systems with general time delays
item.description: arXiv:2609.05726v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a class of infinite dimensional linear port-Hamiltonian delay systems, give a characterization for such systems, and provide an easily verifiable sufficient condition to belong to this class, thereby extending the study by Breiten, Hinsen and Unger in [IEEE Trans. Autom. Control vol. 69, no. 12 (2024), pp. 8924-8930, doi: 10.1109/TAC.2024.3464332]. The results rely on the operator semigroup theoretic treatment of linear delay PDEs.
item.dc:creator: Rogelio Arancibia Bustos, B\'alint Farkas, Birgit Jacob, Merlin Schmitz

item.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.14074v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets. Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.
item.dc:creator: Mar\'ia V. Ferrer, Salvador Hern\'andez, Isabel Sep\'ulveda

item.title: A positive version of Miljutin's Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2609.14148v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we provide a positive version of Miljutin's theorem. Namely, we show that for any uncountable compact metric spaces $K$ and $L$ there exists a positive isomorphism $T:C(K)\longrightarrow C(L)$. Moreover, the inverse of $T$ is a regular operator, and $T$ may be chosen so that $\|T\|_\mathrm{r} \cdot \|T^{-1}\|_\mathrm{r} \leq 9+6\sqrt3$. The method also gives positive versions of classical nonmetrizable results for Miljutin and Dugundji compacta. In particular, if $G$ and $H$ are infinite compact groups of the same weight, then $C(G)$ and $C(H)$ are positively and regularly isomorphic with the same uniform quantitative estimate.
item.dc:creator: Javier Laguna-Ricart, Gonzalo Mart\'inez-Cervantes, Jakub Rondo\v{s}, Alberto Salguero-Alarc\'on

item.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carath\'eodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.12797v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $\sigma$-complete, lattice-$\sigma$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Reggiolli Teixeira

item.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13596v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,\lambda \in (0,1)$: \[ \gamma_{\Sigma_1}(K)^{1-p} \gamma_{\Sigma_2}(L)^p \le \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-\lambda} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}{\lambda} \right)^p \right)^{n} \gamma_{\Gamma}((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L) , \] whenever $\Gamma \leq \Sigma_1 \sharp_p \Sigma_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \Gamma$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=\lambda$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: \[ \gamma(a K)^{1-\lambda} \gamma(b L)^{\lambda} \leq \gamma \left ( a^{1-\lambda} b^\lambda \left ((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Milman, Shohei Nakamura, Hiroshi Tsuji

item.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.37035v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}^k$ on $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<\alpha\leq1$. We also show that, for every $\alpha>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.
item.dc:creator: Shibo Xu, Tao Yu

item.title: Distributionally robust approximation property of neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2510.09177v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The universal approximation property uniformly with respect to weakly compact families of measures is established for several classes of neural networks. To that end, we prove that these neural networks are dense in Orlicz spaces, thereby extending classical universal approximation theorems even beyond the traditional $L^p$-setting. The covered classes of neural networks include widely used architectures like feedforward neural networks with non-polynomial activation functions, deep narrow networks with ReLU activation functions and functional input neural networks.
item.dc:creator: Mihriban Ceylan, David J. Pr\"omel

item.title: Global Well-Posedness of the Vacuum Free Boundary Problem for the Degenerate Compressible Navier-Stokes Equations With Large Data of Spherical Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2601.06620v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The study of global-in-time dynamics of vacuum is crucial for understanding viscous flows. In particular, physical vacuum, which ensures a finite, nontrivial pressure-induced acceleration in the normal direction on the moving boundary, naturally arises in the motion of gaseous stars and shallow water. The corresponding large-data problems for spherically symmetric flows remain open, due to the combined difficulties of coordinate singularity at the origin and degeneracy on the moving boundary. In this paper, we analyze the free boundary problem for the barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with density-dependent viscosity coefficients (as in the shallow water equations) in two and three spatial dimensions. For a general class of spherically symmetric initial densities: $\rho_0^{\beta}\in H^3$ with $\beta\in (\frac{1}{3},\gamma-1]$ ($\gamma$: adiabatic exponent), vanishing on the moving boundary in the form of a distance function, we establish the global existence of the unique classical solution with large data. Moreover, our solution is classical up to the moving boundary, and the physical vacuum is allowed for the data under consideration here when $\beta=\gamma-1$. The key ingredient of our analysis is to obtain the uniform control over the first-order spatial derivatives of the flow map $\eta(t,r)$ in spherically symmetric Lagrangian coordinates, which is achieved by some novel density-weighted estimates and flow-map-weighted estimates for the solutions.
item.dc:creator: Gui-Qiang G. Chen, Jiawen Zhang, Shengguo Zhu

item.title: Debiasing optimal transport: classical and entropic
item.description: arXiv:2604.19981v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the notion of debiasability for cost functions arising in optimal transport. We call a symmetric cost function $c:\mathscr{X}\times\mathscr{X}\to R\cup\{+\infty\}$ debiasable if it satisfies $c(x,y)\ge \tfrac{1}{2}c(x,x)+\tfrac{1}{2}c(y,y)$ for all $x,y\in\mathscr{X}$. Building on an equivalent characterization by an inf-representation $c(x,y)=\inf_{z\in\mathscr Z}\psi(x,z)+\psi(y,z)$ for some set $\mathscr Z$ and some function $\psi:\mathscr X\times\mathscr Z\to R\cup\{+\infty\}$, interpreted as a generalization of the midpoint identity for squared geodesic distances, we investigate the debiasability of costs defined on spaces of probability measures. Our primary focus is the entropic regularization of optimal transport across the different regimes of the regularization parameter $\varepsilon\in[0,+\infty]$, encompassing classical optimal transport ($\varepsilon=0$), entropic optimal transport ($\varepsilon>0$), and the Maximum Mean Discrepancy ($\varepsilon=+\infty$). For $\varepsilon\in(0,+\infty)$ we obtain debiasability under negative definiteness of the ground cost, through an explicit Gaussian factorization, and, more generally, under positive semidefiniteness of the kernel $e^{-c/\varepsilon}$ alone, conditions also proved necessary. All our results extend naturally to unbalanced optimal transport settings. Extending our factorizations to include a time parameter $t\in(0,1)$, we construct an entropic interpolation curve given by an intermediate measure $\eta_t\in\mathscr P(\mathscr Z)$ based on a barycentric formulation, which coincides with the marginals of the Schr\"odinger bridge between $\mu$ and $\nu$. As a byproduct, we derive a new proof for the entropic Benamou-Brenier formula under very mild assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Cyril Aubin-Frankowski, Virginie Ehrlacher, Gabriele Todeschi

item.title: UCP Maps on Finite Toeplitz Systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.02561v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study unital completely positive (UCP) maps on the finite Toeplitz operator system $\mathcal T_d$ of $d \times d$ Toeplitz matrices. We give an explicit characterization of pure UCP maps on $\mathcal T_d$ taking values in $M_n$ in terms of positive $n\times n$ matrix-valued trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $d-1$. This characterization yields a checkable criterion for deciding whether a given UCP map is pure. As an application, we prove that every pure UCP map on $\mathcal T_d$ has a unique completely positive extension to the generated $C^*$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Ritul Duhan, Abhay Jindal

item.title: The point-cross dimension
item.description: arXiv:2607.08612v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two transverse segments have local Hausdorff and upper box dimension one at their crossing, although they carry two independent tangent directions. We define the Point-Cross Dimension by assigning each tangent line the largest local upper box dimension captured by intersection with a regular \(C^1\) curve in that direction, then taking the supremum of their sums over finite independent families of tangent lines. Every Bouligand direction admits such a recurrent curve. The resulting profile is invariant under closure and covariant under local \(C^1\)-diffeomorphisms. Each directional weight is attained, and the profile is upper semicontinuous. An integral representation by ranks of weight superlevel sets gives submodularity and, together with projection bounds, exact Cartesian-product additivity. Germs with the same projective tangent support, local upper box dimension, and rank of segment directions can have different Point-Cross Dimensions. Further computations give exact directional profiles for chirps and the Point-Cross Dimension of a self-affine carpet. Finally, approximation of a ray with error \(O(t^d)\), for \(d>1\), forces directional weight at least \(1-1/d\), and this bound is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Nadir Maaroufi

item.title: Real and complex stability radii for a class of transport networks
item.description: arXiv:2607.12812v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We characterize stability and its robustness for a class of boundary controlled, boundary observed hyperbolic partial differential equations. In particular, we show that asymptotic and exponential stability coincide for this class. Furthermore, we introduce the real and complex stability radii for which we give explicit formulas. In addition, we consider the dual system and its application to controllability and observability. Our main results are illustrated with two examples.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hastir, Birgit Jacob, Hannes Wagener

item.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.22277v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.
item.dc:creator: Miguel F. Barea-Fern\'andez, Ron Kerman, Jan Lang, Javier Soria

item.title: Sharp Capacity Estimates and Volume Growth for Fractional Sobolev Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24752v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain sharp two-sided estimates for the relative capacity of fat and thin annuli in the fractional Sobolev spaces $W^s_{p,q}$, where $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,\infty)$, $q\in(0,\infty]$, in terms of an explicit volume growth quantity. The underlying space is a general metric measure space equipped with a doubling and reverse doubling measure. In particular, whenever the capacity is finite, the estimates are independent of the parameter $q$, and in the Ahlfors regular case with $p=q$ they recover Costea's logarithmic law at $sp=Q$. For $p<q$, we also introduce a sharp condition on the measure that is necessary for the existence of admissible functions in the space $W^s_{p,q}$. For thin annuli $(B_r,B_{r+\varepsilon r})$ under an $\eta$-annular decay property, we uncover a purely nonlocal phenomenon: for $sp <\eta$, the capacity remains bounded as $\varepsilon\to 0$, because the limiting competitor $\chi_{B_r}$ already has finite energy, while if $sp\geq\eta$ it blows up as $ \varepsilon\to0$.
item.dc:creator: Angha Agarwal

item.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno
